current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: 2024, 2025, 2026 regular sessions. § 610.026 RSMo was amended by 2025 H.B. 145 & 59, effective 8/28/2025 — the first amendment since 2004; the revisor page (opened 2026-08-20 via the supplied source document) lists exactly two versions (8/28/2004, ended 8/28/2025; 8/28/2025, current) and no enacted-awaiting-effect 2026 version. The 2025 act added the subsec. 2(2) withdrawal regime (90/150-day fee-remittance and clarification-nonresponse withdrawal, mandatory notices, 6-month re-request fee carryover, lawsuit exception). § 610.023 (3-business-day response) opened at revisor.mo.gov: version effective 8/28/2004, untouched by the 2025 act. No administrative rules implement the Sunshine Law's municipal fee provisions — there is no delegation in § 610.026 to any rulemaking body; the AG's Sunshine Law book (opened, ago.mo.gov PDF) is guidance that tracks the statute (including the 2025 text) and adds no figures beyond it. A 2018 bill (HB 2476, 1¢/page) died and is not law. Guidance-vs-law gap: none found — the AG book reproduces the current statute.

resolutions.unit: USD per page (paper copy not larger than 9x14 inches)
resolutions.source_language: Fees for copying public records, except those records restricted under section 32.091, shall not exceed ten cents per page for a paper copy not larger than nine by fourteen inches, with the hourly fee for duplicating time not to exceed the average hourly rate of pay for clerical staff of the public governmental body.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (version effective 8/28/2025; no later amendment as of 2026-08-20)
resolutions.notes: 'Each public governmental body' — binds municipalities and state bodies alike (§ 610.010(4)). City sets its actual rate at or under 10¢. Carve-outs: records restricted under § 32.091 (dept. of revenue), and per Webster Cnty. Abstract Co. v. Atkison, 328 S.W.3d 434 (Mo. App. S.D. 2010), the 'Except as otherwise provided by law' opener lets record-specific fee statutes (e.g., recorder of deeds, § 59.310) displace this ceiling for those records.

resolutions.unit: USD per page (any paper copy not larger than 9x14 inches; no color distinction)
resolutions.source_language: Fees for copying public records, except those records restricted under section 32.091, shall not exceed ten cents per page for a paper copy not larger than nine by fourteen inches, with the hourly fee for duplicating time not to exceed the average hourly rate of pay for clerical staff of the public governmental body.
resolutions.manual_verification: Scope judgment: the statute never mentions color. The plain text covers every 'paper copy not larger than nine by fourteen inches', so a color page ≤9x14 sits under the same 10¢ ceiling; no MO authority found treating color separately.
resolutions.notes: No color-specific rate anywhere in ch. 610, the AG Sunshine Law book, or case law found. 'Pictures ... graphics, illustrations or similar ... visual items' in § 610.026.1(2) covers photographic/graphic ORIGINALS, not a color photocopy of an ordinary paper record.

resolutions.source_language: Fees for providing access to public records maintained on computer facilities, recording tapes or disks, videotapes or films, pictures, maps, slides, graphics, illustrations or similar audio or visual items or devices, and for paper copies larger than nine by fourteen inches shall include only the cost of copies, staff time, which shall not exceed the average hourly rate of pay for staff of the public governmental body required for making copies and programming, if necessary, and the cost of the disk, tape, or other medium used for the duplication.
resolutions.notes: Paper copies larger than 9x14 fall under the § 610.026.1(2) 'shall include only' cost-component formula (copies + capped staff time + medium), not the 10¢ ceiling. The standard is an enumerated actual-cost formula: R.L. Polk & Co. v. Mo. Dep't of Revenue, 309 S.W.3d 881 (Mo. App. W.D. 2010) rejected a uniform flat per-record fee not built from these components.

resolutions.source_language: Fees for maps, blueprints, or plats that require special expertise to duplicate may include the actual rate of compensation for the trained personnel required to duplicate such maps, blueprints, or plats.
resolutions.notes: Two layers: (a) pictures, maps, slides, graphics, films etc. are priced by the § 610.026.1(2) cost-component formula (MO-0023); (b) maps/blueprints/plats needing special expertise may additionally be billed at the ACTUAL rate of compensation of the trained personnel (MO-9002) — an actual-cost standard, no dollar figure. Transcripts are not addressed in ch. 610 (court-reporter transcripts sit outside municipal records).

resolutions.source_language: Fees for copying public records, except those records restricted under section 32.091, shall not exceed ten cents per page for a paper copy not larger than nine by fourteen inches, with the hourly fee for duplicating time not to exceed the average hourly rate of pay for clerical staff of the public governmental body.
resolutions.notes: No graduated per-page bands by volume anywhere in § 610.026 (opened in full), ch. 610, the AG Sunshine Law book, or the cases collected there. The ceiling is a single flat 10¢/page; a city may adopt its own volume tiers under it.

resolutions.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, each public governmental body shall provide access to and, upon request, furnish copies of public records subject to the following:
resolutions.notes: No free-page allowance in § 610.026 (opened in full), ch. 610, or the AG Sunshine Law book. Fees are chargeable from page one; the only relief is the discretionary public-interest waiver (MO-0024/MO-9006).

resolutions.source_language: Research time required for fulfilling records requests may be charged at the actual cost of research time. Based on the scope of the request, the public governmental body shall produce the copies using employees of the body that result in the lowest amount of charges for search, research, and duplication time.
resolutions.notes: Standard: 'actual cost of research time', bounded by the lowest-cost-staff duty (MO-0021/MO-9004: must use employees yielding the lowest charges for search, research and duplication time). Attorney review time is NOT chargeable as research time — Gross v. Parson, 624 S.W.3d 877 (Mo. banc 2021) (MO-9012). Separate duplicating-time labor is capped at the clerical-staff average hourly rate (MO-0019).

resolutions.source_authority: Gross v. Parson, 624 S.W.3d 877 (Mo. banc 2021); § 610.026.1(1), RSMo (searched)
resolutions.source_language: (2021) Section does not authorize a public governmental body to charge attorney review time as research time required for fulfilling records requests. Gross v. Parson, 624 S.W.3d 877 (Mo.banc).
resolutions.manual_verification: Whether NON-attorney staff time spent segregating/redacting closed material qualifies as chargeable 'research time required for fulfilling records requests' is not settled by statute or Gross; needs legal review before a city bills redaction time.
resolutions.notes: § 610.026 sets no distinct review/redaction rate. Gross v. Parson (Mo. banc 2021) holds attorney review of responsive documents for privileged information is not billable as research time (source_language is the revisor's official annotation, quoted verbatim from the opened revisor page; the AG book states the holding the same way). Configure attorney review as non-chargeable; treat any other redaction labor as unresolved.

resolutions.value: average hourly rate of pay for staff of the public governmental body required for making copies and programming (formula, no dollar figure); actual costs for programming beyond the customary and usual level
resolutions.source_language: Fees for providing access to public records maintained on computer facilities ... shall include only the cost of copies, staff time, which shall not exceed the average hourly rate of pay for staff of the public governmental body required for making copies and programming, if necessary, and the cost of the disk, tape, or other medium used for the duplication. ... If programming is required beyond the customary and usual level to comply with a request for records or information, the fees for compliance may include the actual costs of such programming.
resolutions.notes: Two-band structure: ordinary programming staff time capped at the average hourly pay rate of the staff required (a formula ceiling the city instantiates with its own payroll figure, MO-0023); programming beyond the customary and usual level may be billed at actual costs (MO-9003). Ellipsis in source_language spans only the media-type enumeration and the maps/blueprints sentence; both operative clauses are verbatim.

resolutions.value: always (chargeable from the first minute; no page/hour threshold; not paper-only)
resolutions.source_language: Research time required for fulfilling records requests may be charged at the actual cost of research time.
resolutions.notes: Labor (duplicating time, research time, staff time for electronic records/programming) is permissively chargeable with no free-hour or page-count trigger anywhere in § 610.026 (opened in full) and no threshold in the AG book. Applies to paper AND electronic records (subdiv. (2) staff time). Bounds, not triggers: clerical-rate cap on duplicating time (MO-0019), staff-average-rate cap for electronic (MO-0023), lowest-cost-staff duty (MO-0021), attorney review excluded (MO-9012, Gross v. Parson).

resolutions.source_language: Fees for providing access to public records maintained on computer facilities, recording tapes or disks, videotapes or films, pictures, maps, slides, graphics, illustrations or similar audio or visual items or devices, and for paper copies larger than nine by fourteen inches shall include only the cost of copies, staff time, which shall not exceed the average hourly rate of pay for staff of the public governmental body required for making copies and programming, if necessary, and the cost of the disk, tape, or other medium used for the duplication.
resolutions.manual_verification: The zero is inferred: subdiv. (2)'s 'shall include only' enumeration (copies + capped staff time + medium) leaves no overhead/fringe component, and subdiv. (1) fee elements (10¢/page, duplicating time at clerical rate of PAY, research at actual cost) likewise name no overhead multiplier. No express 'no overhead' sentence exists — confirm no AG opinion permits a fringe loading.
resolutions.notes: No overhead or fringe surcharge is authorized anywhere in § 610.026. 'Average hourly rate of PAY' is a wage figure, not a loaded rate. R.L. Polk (Mo. App. W.D. 2010) rejected a flat fee built on broader cost recovery under subdiv. (2). § 610.026.5 further glosses that copying charges stay non-'fees' under Mo. Const. art. X, § 22 only while they 'do not exceed the level necessary to pay ... the costs for providing a service'.

resolutions.source_language: Research time required for fulfilling records requests may be charged at the actual cost of research time.
resolutions.notes: No billing increment or rounding rule in § 610.026 (opened in full), ch. 610, or the AG Sunshine Law book. City sets its own increment; 'actual cost' and the lowest-cost-staff duty (MO-0021) argue against coarse round-ups.

resolutions.source_language: Research time required for fulfilling records requests may be charged at the actual cost of research time.
resolutions.notes: No free-labor-hours allowance per request in § 610.026 (opened in full), ch. 610, or the AG book (contrast e.g. Tenn./Kan. patterns). Labor is chargeable from the first minute; relief only via the discretionary public-interest waiver.

resolutions.source_language: Research time required for fulfilling records requests may be charged at the actual cost of research time.
resolutions.notes: No per-requestor periodic free-time ledger (TX § 552.275 pattern) anywhere in ch. 610 or the AG book. The only per-requestor accumulation device is the NEW 6-month re-request fee carryover (MO-9010), which is a charge, not an allowance.

resolutions.source_language: Prior to producing copies of the requested records, the person requesting the records may request the public governmental body to provide an estimate of the cost to the person requesting the records.
resolutions.notes: Shape: the estimate is REQUESTER-initiated ('may request ... an estimate'); there is NO dollar or hour threshold at which the body must volunteer a cost notice. Engine gate: if the requester asks before production, the body provides an estimate. MO-9005 amends MO-0022 with the now-confirmed verbatim clause (was is_paraphrase=true).

resolutions.unit: calendar days from the body's request for payment (fees ≤ $1,000 | fees > $1,000)
resolutions.source_language: A request for public records to a public governmental body shall be considered withdrawn if the requester fails to remit all fees within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, of a request for payment of the fees by the public governmental body, prior to fulfilling the request.
resolutions.notes: The window attaches to the body's REQUEST FOR PAYMENT (which in practice carries the estimate), not to a bare estimate: remit all fees within 90 days (150 if fees > $1,000) or the request is deemed withdrawn. The payment request must carry the statutory warning notice (MO-9007). State-fixed; a city cannot shorten or extend it. Lawsuit exception: MO-9011.

resolutions.source_language: Prior to producing copies of the requested records, the person requesting the records may request the public governmental body to provide an estimate of the cost to the person requesting the records.
resolutions.notes: No revised-estimate-on-variance requirement (no percentage trigger) in § 610.026 (opened in full), ch. 610, or the AG book.

resolutions.source_language: Prior to producing copies of the requested records, the person requesting the records may request the public governmental body to provide an estimate of the cost to the person requesting the records.
resolutions.notes: No estimate validity period stated. Practically, the 90/150-day remittance window (MO-0026) bounds how long a payment request stays open, and the 6-month carryover (MO-9010) governs pricing of a re-request — but neither is an estimate-validity rule.

resolutions.value: none (no statutory threshold — payment of fees may be requested before fulfilling any request, regardless of amount)
resolutions.source_language: Payment of fees may be requested prior to fulfilling the request.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (version effective 8/28/2025; sentence renumbered as subsec. 2(1) by the 2025 act)
resolutions.notes: Advance payment is unconditionally permitted — no dollar floor triggers or limits it. A city may set its own internal threshold policy under the permission. The 2025 act moved this sentence into subsec. 2(1) (previously subsec. 2).

resolutions.source_language: Payment of fees may be requested prior to fulfilling the request.
resolutions.notes: No deposit cap percentage: the statute permits requesting payment of 'fees' (up to the full amount) in advance, with no half-of-estimate or similar cap anywhere in ch. 610 or the AG book.

resolutions.source_language: Payment of fees may be requested prior to fulfilling the request.
resolutions.notes: Gate shape: the body MAY condition fulfillment on prior payment of all fees ('prior to fulfilling the request'). Discretionary, not mandatory. Nonpayment terminal outcome: deemed withdrawn at 90/150 days (MO-0026).

resolutions.value: withdrawn after 90 | 150; re-request within 6 months may be charged the expired request's fees plus new fees
resolutions.unit: calendar days from the request for payment (fees ≤ $1,000 | fees > $1,000); months for the carryover window
resolutions.source_language: A request for public records to a public governmental body shall be considered withdrawn if the requester fails to remit all fees within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, of a request for payment of the fees by the public governmental body, prior to fulfilling the request. The public governmental body shall include notice to the requester that if the requester fails to remit payment of the fees within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, then the request for public records shall be considered withdrawn.
resolutions.notes: NEW 2025 regime, state-fixed: (1) deemed-withdrawn at 90 days (150 if fees > $1,000) after a payment request; (2) the payment request MUST carry the warning notice (MO-9007); (3) substantially-similar re-request within 6 months may be charged the original expired fees plus new fees (MO-9010); (4) none of it applies once a lawsuit is filed over the records (MO-9011). Transition clause (requests pending 8/28/2025 → pay by 1/1/2026) is now spent.

resolutions.source_language: Payment of fees may be requested prior to fulfilling the request. ... A request for public records to a public governmental body shall be considered withdrawn if the requester fails to remit all fees within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, of a request for payment of the fees by the public governmental body, prior to fulfilling the request.
resolutions.manual_verification: Interaction between the § 610.023.3 three-business-day response duty and withheld production pending payment is not expressly resolved: the statute states no toll/pause. § 610.023.3 (opened at revisor.mo.gov) requires the request be 'acted upon as soon as possible, but in no event later than the end of the third business day' and allows production to 'exceed three days for reasonable cause'. Legal review before configuring any clock pause.
resolutions.notes: Shape for the engine: no statutory tolling or grace period while payment is outstanding; the body may lawfully withhold FULFILLMENT until fees are paid (MO-0025), while the 3-business-day duty to act on/respond to the request runs independently. Lapse action is statutory and terminal: deemed withdrawn at 90/150 days (MO-0026), preceded by the mandatory warning notice (MO-9007).

resolutions.source_language: Prior to producing copies of the requested records, the person requesting the records may request the public governmental body to provide an estimate of the cost to the person requesting the records.
resolutions.notes: No overrun/re-issue rule: nothing requires a revised estimate when actual cost exceeds the estimate, blocks collecting the overage, or restarts the 90/150-day window on a revised payment request. Coverage: § 610.026 in full, ch. 610, AG book.
out of scope per owner decision 2026-08-20 — finance-department policy, excluded from state rules profile

resolutions.source_language: Based on the scope of the request, the public governmental body shall produce the copies using employees of the body that result in the lowest amount of charges for search, research, and duplication time.
resolutions.manual_verification: No request-level dollar cap exists; the 'cap' is structural (component ceilings + lowest-cost-staff duty + cost-recovery gloss). Confirm no AG opinion imposes an aggregate cap.
resolutions.notes: No total-fee dollar maximum per request. The effective ceiling is the sum of the component limits (10¢/page, clerical-rate duplicating time, actual-cost research, 'include only' components for electronic/oversized) discharged through the mandatory lowest-cost-staff duty. § 610.026.5 keeps copying charges within 'the level necessary to pay ... the costs for providing a service' (Mo. Const. art. X, § 22 gloss).

resolutions.source_language: Documents may be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge when the public governmental body determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the public governmental body and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester;
resolutions.notes: No de-minimis dollar threshold below which charging is barred or waived. A city may implement one under the discretionary public-interest waiver (MO-0024/MO-9006), but the statute names no figure.

resolutions.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, each public governmental body shall provide access to and, upon request, furnish copies of public records subject to the following:
resolutions.notes: No minimum fee in ch. 610 or the AG book. A flat minimum untethered from the cost components would be suspect under R.L. Polk (Mo. App. W.D. 2010, flat per-record fee not authorized under § 610.026.1(2)).

resolutions.source_language: Fees for providing access to public records maintained on computer facilities, recording tapes or disks, videotapes or films, pictures, maps, slides, graphics, illustrations or similar audio or visual items or devices, and for paper copies larger than nine by fourteen inches shall include only the cost of copies, staff time, which shall not exceed the average hourly rate of pay for staff of the public governmental body required for making copies and programming, if necessary, and the cost of the disk, tape, or other medium used for the duplication.
resolutions.notes: Medium charge = 'the cost of the disk, tape, or other medium used for the duplication' — actual cost, no fixed rate. A flat uniform per-copy media fee not built from the three components is unlawful: R.L. Polk & Co. v. Mo. Dep't of Revenue, 309 S.W.3d 881 (Mo. App. W.D. 2010).

resolutions.source_language: Fees for providing access to public records maintained on computer facilities ... shall include only the cost of copies, staff time ... and the cost of the disk, tape, or other medium used for the duplication.
resolutions.notes: No postage/mailing/handling/e-delivery charge provision in § 610.026 (opened in full), ch. 610, or the AG book. Note the tension for electronic/oversized records: the 'shall include only' enumeration does not list postage — whether actual postage may be added for those record classes needs legal review before charging (flagged in gaps).

resolutions.source_language: Except as otherwise provided by law, each public governmental body shall provide access to and, upon request, furnish copies of public records subject to the following:
resolutions.notes: The Sunshine Law sets no certified-copy fee for municipal records generally. Officer-specific statutes outside ch. 610 set certification fees for particular custodians (e.g., recorder of deeds, § 59.310), and per Webster Cnty. Abstract (Mo. App. S.D. 2010) the 'Except as otherwise provided by law' opener lets those control for their records — but no general municipal certification figure exists.

resolutions.source_language: Fees for providing access to public records maintained on computer facilities, recording tapes or disks, videotapes or films, pictures, maps, slides, graphics, illustrations or similar audio or visual items or devices, and for paper copies larger than nine by fourteen inches shall include only the cost of copies, staff time, which shall not exceed the average hourly rate of pay for staff of the public governmental body required for making copies and programming, if necessary, and the cost of the disk, tape, or other medium used for the duplication.
resolutions.notes: Audio/video ('recording tapes or disks, videotapes or films ... similar audio or visual items') priced by the same three-component actual-cost formula: copies + staff time (capped at staff average hourly pay rate) + medium. No per-recording flat rate, no per-minute rate, no free minutes anywhere in ch. 610 or the AG book.

resolutions.source_language: Documents may be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge when the public governmental body determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the public governmental body and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester;
resolutions.notes: No commercial-purpose surcharge or separate schedule: the same fee limits apply regardless of purpose. 'Commercial interest' appears only as a DISQUALIFIER for the public-interest waiver (MO-9006) — a waiver limiter, not a fee schedule.

resolutions.source_language: Documents may be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge when the public governmental body determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the public governmental body and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester;
resolutions.notes: Shape: DISCRETIONARY waiver/reduction; grounds = public interest via significant contribution to public understanding of the body's operations AND not primarily in the requester's commercial interest. No purpose-statement requirement on requesters, no written-denial duty for waiver refusals (the § 610.023.4 written-denial duty covers denial of ACCESS, not waiver denials), no waiver-specific appeal, no indigency waiver. MO-9006 amends MO-0024 to carry the full verbatim clause including the commercial-interest limiter.

resolutions.source_language: Each request for access to a public record shall be acted upon as soon as possible, but in no event later than the end of the third business day following the date the request is received by the custodian of records of a public governmental body.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (§ 610.023 version effective 8/28/2004, unchanged by the 2025 act)
resolutions.notes: No fee-forfeiture-on-late-response rule. § 610.023.3 (opened at revisor.mo.gov) sets the 3-business-day duty with no fee consequence for missing it; late-response remedies run through § 610.027 civil penalties/attorney fees (out of scope), not fee forfeiture. AG book confirms no such rule.

resolutions.source_language: If the same or a substantially similar request for public records is made within six months after the expiration of the ninety-day period, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, and no fee was remitted for such request or no response was received to the request for clarification, then the public governmental body may request payment of the same fees made for the original request that has expired in addition to any allowable fees necessary to fulfill the subsequent request.
resolutions.notes: NEW 2025 fee CARRYOVER (not aggregation): a same/substantially-similar re-request within 6 months after a 90/150-day withdrawal (nonpayment OR clarification nonresponse, MO-9008) may be charged the expired request's fees PLUS the new request's fees. Permissive. Requestor-ledger shape (match prior withdrawn requests per requestor). No fee-aggregation-across-requests threshold exists. Lawsuit exception: MO-9011.

new_rules.legal_concept: Oversized paper copies (larger than 9x14) priced by cost components
new_rules.atomic_rule: Fees for paper copies larger than nine by fourteen inches shall include only the cost of copies, staff time (not exceeding the average hourly rate of pay for staff required for making copies and programming), and the cost of the medium used for the duplication.
new_rules.trigger: Producing a paper copy larger than 9x14 inches
new_rules.source_language: Fees for providing access to public records maintained on computer facilities, recording tapes or disks, videotapes or films, pictures, maps, slides, graphics, illustrations or similar audio or visual items or devices, and for paper copies larger than nine by fourteen inches shall include only the cost of copies, staff time, which shall not exceed the average hourly rate of pay for staff of the public governmental body required for making copies and programming, if necessary, and the cost of the disk, tape, or other medium used for the duplication.
new_rules.notes: Extracted because MO-0023's row named only electronic/media records; the same clause expressly covers oversized paper copies, which the prior pass left silent. ceiling: enumerated actual-cost components only.

new_rules.legal_concept: Maps/blueprints/plats requiring special expertise — trained-personnel compensation
new_rules.atomic_rule: Fees for maps, blueprints, or plats that require special expertise to duplicate may include the actual rate of compensation for the trained personnel required to duplicate them.
new_rules.trigger: Duplicating maps, blueprints, or plats that require special expertise
new_rules.source_language: Fees for maps, blueprints, or plats that require special expertise to duplicate may include the actual rate of compensation for the trained personnel required to duplicate such maps, blueprints, or plats.
new_rules.notes: ceiling: actual rate of compensation of the trained personnel (an actual-cost bound, no dollar figure). Lifts the default staff-average-rate cap for this record class only.

new_rules.legal_concept: Programming beyond the customary and usual level — actual costs
new_rules.atomic_rule: If programming beyond the customary and usual level is required to comply with a request, the fees may include the actual costs of such programming.
new_rules.trigger: Request requires programming beyond the customary and usual level
new_rules.source_language: If programming is required beyond the customary and usual level to comply with a request for records or information, the fees for compliance may include the actual costs of such programming.
new_rules.notes: ceiling: actual programming costs; exceeds the ordinary staff-average-rate cap (MO-0023) only when the programming is beyond customary/usual. Secondary rule type: Calculation.

new_rules.atomic_rule: Based on the scope of the request, the public governmental body shall produce the copies using employees of the body that result in the lowest amount of charges for search, research, and duplication time.
new_rules.trigger: Assigning staff to fulfill a copy request
new_rules.source_language: Based on the scope of the request, the public governmental body shall produce the copies using employees of the body that result in the lowest amount of charges for search, research, and duplication time.
new_rules.notes: Amends MO-0021 (was is_paraphrase=true / 'Requires manual verification'): operative clause now confirmed verbatim from the opened current statute. It is a mandatory duty ('shall produce'), scoped by 'Based on the scope of the request'. Config home corrected to structural — it is a cost-minimization duty the engine applies, not a value the city fills in.

new_rules.legal_concept: Requester-initiated cost estimate before production (verbatim confirmation)
new_rules.atomic_rule: Prior to producing copies, the person requesting the records may request the public governmental body to provide an estimate of the cost.
new_rules.trigger: Requester asks for a cost estimate before copies are produced
new_rules.source_language: Prior to producing copies of the requested records, the person requesting the records may request the public governmental body to provide an estimate of the cost to the person requesting the records.
new_rules.notes: Amends MO-0022 (was is_paraphrase=true / 'Requires manual verification'): clause confirmed verbatim from the opened current statute. Estimate is requester-initiated; no threshold obliges the body to volunteer one.

new_rules.legal_concept: Public-interest fee waiver with commercial-interest limiter (full verbatim)
new_rules.atomic_rule: The body may furnish documents without charge or at a reduced charge when it determines the waiver or reduction is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the body's operations or activities and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester.
new_rules.trigger: Body determines waiver/reduction is in the public interest and not primarily in the requester's commercial interest
new_rules.source_language: Documents may be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge when the public governmental body determines that waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest because it is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of the operations or activities of the public governmental body and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester;
new_rules.notes: Amends MO-0024: its source_language omitted the conjunctive second ground 'and is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester' — a waiver DISQUALIFIER the engine must test. Both grounds are conjunctive; do not fragment. Whether the commercial-interest clause predates the 2025 act was not determined from the prior-version text (flagged in gaps); the current operative text is verbatim.

new_rules.legal_concept: Mandatory withdrawal-warning notice in the request for payment
new_rules.atomic_rule: When requesting payment of fees, the public governmental body shall include notice to the requester that failure to remit payment within ninety days (one hundred fifty days if the requested fees exceed one thousand dollars) makes the request considered withdrawn.
new_rules.trigger: Body issues a request for payment of fees
new_rules.source_language: The public governmental body shall include notice to the requester that if the requester fails to remit payment of the fees within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, then the request for public records shall be considered withdrawn.
new_rules.notes: NEW 2025. Required notice content on every fee/payment request; the withdrawal clock (MO-0026) presumably depends on a compliant notice — statute does not state the consequence of an omitted notice (flagged in gaps).

new_rules.legal_concept: Clarification nonresponse — request deemed withdrawn (90/150 days)
new_rules.atomic_rule: If the body seeks clarification of a request and receives no response within ninety days (one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars) of sending the clarification request, the request is considered withdrawn.
new_rules.trigger: Body sends a clarification request; no response received within 90/150 days
new_rules.clock_spec: 90 calendar-days from sending the clarification request (150 calendar-days if requested fees > $1,000); expiry = request considered withdrawn
new_rules.source_language: If the public governmental body responds to a request for public records in order to seek a clarification of the request and no response to the request for clarification is received by the public governmental body within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, of sending the request for clarification, then such request for public records shall be considered withdrawn.
new_rules.notes: NEW 2025. Sits in the fee section and keys its 150-day variant to the requested FEES exceeding $1,000, but operates as a clarification-abandonment clock. Concept key proposed (clarification.nonresponse_abandonment) — not among the 23 supplied fee/payment concepts; map to the master dictionary's clarification family at reconcile.

new_rules.legal_concept: Mandatory withdrawal-warning notice in the clarification request
new_rules.atomic_rule: The body's request for clarification shall include notice that failure to respond within ninety days (one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars) makes the request considered withdrawn.
new_rules.trigger: Body issues a request for clarification
new_rules.source_language: The request for clarification by the public governmental body shall include notice to the requester that if the requester fails to respond within ninety days, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, then the request shall be considered withdrawn.
new_rules.notes: NEW 2025. Companion notice duty to MO-9008.

new_rules.legal_concept: Six-month re-request fee carryover after withdrawal
new_rules.atomic_rule: If the same or a substantially similar request is made within six months after expiration of the 90/150-day period and no fee was remitted (or no clarification response received), the body may request payment of the original expired request's fees in addition to any allowable fees for the subsequent request.
new_rules.trigger: Same/substantially similar request within 6 months after a 90/150-day withdrawal for nonpayment or clarification nonresponse
new_rules.source_language: If the same or a substantially similar request for public records is made within six months after the expiration of the ninety-day period, or within one hundred fifty days if the requested fees are greater than one thousand dollars, and no fee was remitted for such request or no response was received to the request for clarification, then the public governmental body may request payment of the same fees made for the original request that has expired in addition to any allowable fees necessary to fulfill the subsequent request.
new_rules.notes: NEW 2025. Requestor-ledger structural rule: requires matching a new request against the requestor's withdrawn requests from the prior 6 months and carrying the expired fees forward. 'Same or a substantially similar' is a soft standard — do not automate the similarity judgment; human confirms the match.

new_rules.legal_concept: Lawsuit exception to the withdrawal regime
new_rules.atomic_rule: The subsec. 2(2) withdrawal provisions do not apply if a lawsuit has been filed against the public governmental body with regard to the records that are the subject of the request.
new_rules.trigger: A lawsuit is filed against the body regarding the requested records
new_rules.clock_spec: undefined-soft: withdrawal regime 'shall not apply' while a lawsuit regarding the records is filed — no day-count; disables the 90/150-day terminal clocks
new_rules.source_language: The provisions of this subdivision shall not apply if a lawsuit has been filed against the public governmental body with regard to the records that are the subject of the request under this subdivision.
new_rules.notes: NEW 2025. Disables the entire subdivision (withdrawal, notices, carryover) once litigation over the records is filed. Clock effect recorded as pauses in the sense of disabling the terminal clocks; statute does not say whether they resume post-suit (flagged in gaps).

new_rules.legal_concept: Attorney review time not chargeable as research time
new_rules.atomic_rule: A public governmental body may not charge attorney review time (review of responsive documents for privileged information) as research time under § 610.026.1(1).
new_rules.trigger: Attorney reviews responsive documents in fulfilling a request
new_rules.source_language: (2021) Section does not authorize a public governmental body to charge attorney review time as research time required for fulfilling records requests. Gross v. Parson, 624 S.W.3d 877 (Mo.banc).
new_rules.notes: Source language is the revisor's official case annotation on the opened § 610.026 page, quoted verbatim (it is the annotation's text, not the opinion's own words); AG Sunshine book states the holding identically ('does not include time for attorney to review responsive documents for privileged information'). Narrow holding only — does not decide non-attorney redaction time.

delegations_followed.statute_cite: § 610.026, RSMo (timing context for fee gates; not a fee delegation — no rulemaking delegation exists in the MO fee section)
delegations_followed.instrument: § 610.023, RSMo (response deadlines; cross-referenced statute opened for timing-linked items per state note)
delegations_followed.figures_extracted: 3 business days to act on a request (extendable for reasonable cause with detailed explanation); written denial grounds within 3 business days of request for the statement. No fee forfeiture, no clock-toll-on-nonpayment provision. Version effective 8/28/2004 — unchanged by 2025 H.B. 145 & 59.

applicability_notes: § 610.026 binds 'each public governmental body' — the § 610.010(4) definition includes municipal legislative and administrative bodies, so every figure here applies to municipalities and state bodies alike (applies_to = all_public_bodies). Missouri has no separate state-agency uniform fee schedule for Sunshine requests.

The 'Except as otherwise provided by law' opener is operative: record-specific fee statutes outside ch. 610 displace the § 610.026 limits for their records (Webster Cnty. Abstract Co. v. Atkison, 328 S.W.3d 434 (Mo. App. S.D. 2010) — recorder of deeds per-page fees under § 59.310 controlled). A city configuring department-specific schedules (recorder, police reports under other statutes) may lawfully diverge from the 10¢ ceiling only where such a statute exists.
Records restricted under § 32.091 (department of revenue motor-vehicle/driver records) are carved out of the 10¢ paper ceiling — state-agency matter, noted only.

§ 610.026.3 vs .4: state bodies remit fee revenue to state general revenue; political-subdivision bodies (municipalities) remit to their own fiscal officer. Money-routing only — no effect on chargeable amounts.
The subsec. 2(2) transition clause (requests pending on 8/28/2025 withdrawn unless fees remitted by 1/1/2026) is spent as of the research date and was not emitted as a rule row.
material_negatives: No graduated per-page volume tiers, free-page allowance, free labor hours, or per-requestor periodic free time anywhere in ch. 610 or the AG Sunshine Law book.
No labor billing increment/rounding rule; no overhead or fringe surcharge authorization ('average hourly rate of PAY' is an unloaded wage figure).
No mandatory body-initiated estimate threshold, no revised-estimate-on-variance rule, no estimate validity period, no overrun re-issue rule.
No deposit dollar threshold and no deposit percentage cap — advance payment of the full fee may be requested for any request.
No request-level dollar fee cap, de-minimis threshold, or minimum fee.

No postage/delivery charge provision, no certification fee for municipal records generally (officer-specific statutes aside), no commercial-purpose surcharge or schedule, no fee forfeiture on late response, no indigency waiver.
No administrative rules implement the Sunshine Law's fee provisions — § 610.026 delegates nothing to rulemaking; there is no MO fee instrument to open beyond the statute.
gaps_manual_verification: labor.review.rate: whether NON-attorney staff time spent segregating/redacting closed material is chargeable 'research time' is unsettled (Gross v. Parson decided only attorney review). Legal review before billing redaction labor.
labor.overheadPct: the 0% is inferred from the 'shall include only' enumeration and the unloaded pay-rate ceilings, not an express prohibition — confirm no AG opinion allows fringe loading.

payment.depositClock: interaction between withheld production pending payment (§ 610.026.2(1)) and the § 610.023.3 three-business-day duty is not expressly resolved; no statutory toll. Legal review before configuring any clock pause.

MO-9006/waiver: whether the 'not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester' limiter was added by the 2025 act or present since 2004 was not determined (the prior 8/28/2004 revisor version was not opened); the current operative text is verbatim regardless.

MO-9007/MO-9009: the statute does not state the consequence of omitting the mandatory withdrawal-warning notice (does the 90/150-day clock still run?). Treat a compliant notice as a precondition pending legal review.
MO-9011: whether the 90/150-day clocks resume or reset after a lawsuit concludes is unstated.
delivery: whether actual postage may be added for § 610.026.1(2) records despite the 'shall include only' enumeration needs legal review before charging.
certification: officer-specific certification-fee statutes (e.g., § 59.310 recorders) were not inventoried — out of the municipal-general scope; flag for a department-schedule pass.

proposed_concept_keys.definition: A request is deemed withdrawn/abandoned when the requester fails to respond to the body's clarification request within a fixed period (MO: 90 calendar days, or 150 if requested fees exceed $1,000).
